title: Schema envelope, incremental coercion policy, and user-facing remediation protocol for tool/function calls
creator: Ava Chao
description: Define a compact, forward-compatible JSON 'schema envelope' for function/tool calls that supports (1) explicit coercion policies, (2) incremental (streaming) validation hooks, and (3) structured, actionable error codes and remediation text for SDKs and Console. Goal: reduce production type mismatches and make runtime recovery and user guidance deterministic across hosted/dedicated/private modes.
motivation: We see recurring incidents where downstream tool invocations fail due to small shape mismatches (string vs number, missing optional fields) and users get cryptic runtime errors. Streaming responses currently cannot report partial schema problems in a way clients can act on during an ongoing generation session. This work defines the envelope and the runtime handling strategy so SDKs and integrations can implement consistent, human-friendly remediation flows.
acceptance_criteria: Schema envelope spec committed to docs with examples for common patterns (simple, nested, arrays)
Runtime supports three validation modes: strict, permissive, streaming-inspect and behavior described in spec
SDKs (JS + Python) include one example remediation UI snippet that maps error codes to messages
E2E test harness demonstrates automatic coercion for safe cases and clear rejection for unsafe cases with specific error codes
Console surfaces validation errors with remediation hints for at least two sample tools in catalog
design_notes: We introduce a lightweight envelope that sits alongside the existing 'tool' metadata so it is backward compatible. The envelope fields are 'schema', 'coercion', 'validationMode', and 'diagnosticHints'. Key design choices: prefer explicit flags over heuristics; make coercion opt-in per-field; provide stable error codes for client mapping; support streaming validation that emits incremental diagnostic frames without breaking token streaming.
schema_envelope_proposal: Top-level envelope keys: 'paramsSchema' (JSON Schema Draft-2020-12 subset), 'x-redwood-coercion' (object with per-field rules), 'validationMode' ("strict"|"permissive"|"streaming-inspect"), 'diagnosticHints' (array of short strings). Rationale: embeds policy next to schema so runtime can deterministically decide when to coerce vs when to error.
coercion_policy_examples: Global policy 'allowImplicitCoercion': false by default for security-sensitive tools (payment, billing)
validation_mode_semantics: strict: validate against schema and reject on first mismatch with RWD-VAL-4xx codes
permissive: attempt safe coercions defined in 'x-redwood-coercion' and only error for unsafe mismatches

streaming-inspect: perform best-effort incremental validation during generation and emit 'validation-frame' diagnostics interleaved with token stream (non-blocking). A final validation outcome is returned at the end of the call.
error_taxonomy_snippets: RWD-VAL-001: missing_required_field - remediation: 'Add field "{field}" of type {type}. See example payload in docs.'
RWD-VAL-012: type_mismatch_coercible - remediation: 'Service converted field "{field}" from {fromType} to {toType}. To prevent automatic coercion, set coercion to none in the schema.'
RWD-VAL-020: type_mismatch_non_coercible - remediation: 'Field "{field}" must be {type}. Provide a value that matches the expected type or update the tool schema.'
RWD-VAL-030: json_parse_error - remediation: 'Ensure nested JSON fields are valid JSON or mark as string and parse client-side.'

RWD-VAL-050: streaming_partial_warning - remediation: 'Partial shape detected during streaming; validate final payload after completion. If you need strict streaming validation, switch to validationMode="strict".'
runtime_behavior_notes: During permissive mode the runtime records any coercions applied in a 'coercionAudit' list that is attached to the final response metadata. For streaming-inspect the runtime emits diagnostic frames with type 'schema.diagnostic' containing short codes and human hints; these frames are dropped if client does not accept diagnostic frames. Backwards compatibility: if no envelope present, treat calls as 'permissive' but do not apply implicit coercions for security-labeled tools.
implementation_plan: 1) Spec draft + examples committed to docs. 2) Runtime: implement envelope parsing, integrate with existing parameter marshaling, add coercion hooks and diagnostic frame emitter. 3) SDKs: add high-level helpers to surface error codes and remediation. 4) Console: error UI treatment and link to schema authoring tool. 5) QA: run compatibility tests with legacy tools and simulate token streaming with injected partial shapes.
test_cases: Missing required top-level field => RWD-VAL-001 (strict), permissive mode should fail too
Number passed as string with coercion flag => success + RWD-VAL-012 logging
Array passed as csv string with csv-to-array coercion => success
Unsafe shape change (object->primitive) => RWD-VAL-020 and call rejected
Streaming session with intermediate type drift => emit RWD-VAL-050 frames and final outcome
rollout_notes: Stage 1: opt-in feature flag for 'schema_envelope' accepted by runtime. Stage 2: default expose validationMode=permissive for new tools and surface audit logs. Stage 3: migration guide for existing tool authors to explicitly adopt envelope and coercion flags. Communicate breaking behaviors for strict mode only.
monitoring_and_alerting: Track rate of RWD-VAL-020 and RWD-VAL-001 errors per tool and per customer. Create alert when one customer sees >0.5% of calls rejected due to non-coercible type mismatches. Add dashboard tile for coercionAudit prevalence.
outstanding_decisions: Do we accept JSON Schema Draft-2020-12 subset or design a smaller ad-hoc schema? (current lean: adopt subset to reduce authoring burden)
How to represent field-level sensitivity to prevent coercion for security sensitive types? (proposal: schema meta 'sensitive': true)
Should diagnostic frames be encrypted or redacted for private deployments? (security review pending)
notes_from_review: PM (Lina Park): prefer conservative defaults for coercion to avoid silent bugs in customer invoicing flows
Design (Rashid Khan): console should show a one-click 'preview coerced payload' action when an audit exists
Security (Isha Patel): request: add 'sensitive' flag handling in spec and mark security_review_required=true for tools annotated with 'payment' or 'secrets' labels
